checked.what_was_checked: Arm-to-seat bindings, complete parent/child cost accounting, separation of seat effects from spawn/fork/cache effects, task-scope attribution, and cache-order effects.

Measured-versus-modelled host units, item and repetition denominators, aggregation of cost per verified item, matched fixture populations, and exclusions. The design correctly avoids averaging Claude measured dollars with Codex modelled dollars, but other bases are not pinned.

Known-opposite, denominator, seat-receipt, zero-detection, cliff, known-bad, fixture-freshness, Codex cache-key, and Claude TTL controls. Seat mismatches and cliff-only savings are visibly caught; the findings concern controls that can pass or fail for the wrong reason.
Stage-1 screening, Stage-2 confirmation, 20%/25% decision boundaries, quality non-inferiority, aggregation, sampling noise, multiplicity, and which arms are eligible for each decision.

Claims about the prior N values, fork mechanisms, Codex dispatch accounting, and the bundled Claude parser. The bare-object/list claim for `_parse_claude` is supported by the excerpt; other contradictions appear below.
Internal rate arithmetic, output-dominance rationale, cache-prefix application, long-context handling, TTL asymmetries, and the Codex-to-Claude staging inference.

findings.anchor_quote: | Arm | inline · delegated-cheap (effort low) · delegated-cheap (effort high) · delegated-mid · fork-same · fork-cheap (Codex only) |
findings.input_or_condition: The implementation chooses any plausible but unregistered binding, such as Claude `cheap` being sweep/haiku versus workhorse/opus, or inline being opus versus fable, with unspecified inline and mid effort.
findings.signal_emitted: A result is reported as the economics of `delegated-cheap`, `delegated-mid`, or the shipped cheap seats.
findings.truth_instead: It is only the result for the implementation-time binding selected; another binding represented by the same arm label can have a different cost and quality result.
findings.evidence: The rate table supplies four Claude models and three GPT models, while Bundle 1 binds SWEEP and WORKHORSE differently. The arm table never assigns agent type, parent model, child model, or all efforts per host.
findings.change_required: Replace the abstract arm labels with a per-host treatment matrix fixing parent agent/model/effort, child agent/model/effort, fork mechanism, fan-out count, and the exact receipt expected for every arm.

findings.anchor_quote: | Arm | inline · delegated-cheap (effort low) · delegated-cheap (effort high) · delegated-mid · fork-same · fork-cheap (Codex only) |
findings.input_or_condition: Delegated-cheap beats inline because the delegated route avoids prior-turn thinking, uses a shorter child context, or receives fan-out cache reuse, even though changing the model contributes no saving.
findings.signal_emitted: The ≥25% contrast is presented as a cheap-seat advantage and triggers KEEP.
findings.truth_instead: The advantage is caused by the routing mechanism; the same-model isolated spawn could provide it without retaining a cheap seat.
findings.evidence: The design itself says prior-turn thinking taxes inline but not delegated runs and that fan-out changes cache-write economics. There is no isolated delegated arm on the inline model and effort; `fork-same` changes packet and cache inheritance simultaneously.
findings.change_required: Add an isolated delegated-same-model-and-effort arm with the same packet and fan-out as delegated-cheap, and base seat attribution on cheap versus delegated-same rather than cheap versus inline alone.

findings.anchor_quote: - **Codex** — an OAuth subscription pays no per-run dollar. Tokens by kind are measured;
findings.input_or_condition: Codex top-level `turn.completed` usage excludes one or more spawned-child rollouts, and the run cost is computed from only the top-level dispatch.
findings.signal_emitted: The delegated arm emits a low modelled total and appears cheaper because the child ran on a cheap seat.
findings.truth_instead: The modelled total omitted the child's work; full route cost is the parent brief and acceptance plus every child or fork request.
findings.evidence: Bundle 2 describes Codex usage as per-turn and per-dispatch. The target separately reads a child's own rollout and first request, proving participant records exist, but it specifies no accounting-closure assertion joining them into the run total.
findings.change_required: Require a run ledger that receipts the parent and every expected child/fork, sums every participant from brief through acceptance, and fails cost publication unless participant counts and usage reconcile.

findings.anchor_quote: Whether agent-bios ships cheap seats (`workhorse`, `sweep`) as spawn targets at all, and
findings.input_or_condition: Stage 2 finds no write-task saving and the DELETE branch is applied to both `workhorse` and `sweep`.
findings.signal_emitted: The experiment says both cheap spawn targets should be deleted.
findings.truth_instead: The experiment exercises the workhorse write contract only; it supplies no valid result for sweep's intended read-dominated role, and the target itself identifies workhorse as the write-capable seat.
findings.evidence: Under Why this exists, the target calls workhorse the only spawn target without `disallowedTools` and the write-capable seat. Under Task, it says the fixture exercises the workhorse contract.
findings.change_required: Restrict this experiment and its delete threshold to write-capable workhorse seats. Require a separate read-only, sweep-contract experiment before permitting deletion of `sweep`.

findings.anchor_quote: is code the agent writes.
findings.input_or_condition: The recorded token-cost breakdown shows cache writes, uncached input, cache reads, and prior reasoning account for most billed cost, as can occur for L3 adjacent-module reads or large injected corpora.
findings.signal_emitted: The threshold result is labelled evidence about write-dominated work.
findings.truth_instead: A task containing edits is not necessarily output-dominated; that run measured another input/cache-dominated workload.
findings.evidence: The design records five billed token kinds, states every spawn writes the instruction corpus, and requires L3 to read an adjacent module, but gives no measured output-share eligibility rule.
findings.change_required: Define output dominance quantitatively before running and make it a cell-validity gate using the measured token-cost shares; relabel or reject cells that do not meet it.

findings.anchor_quote: input-dominated, and the price gap between tiers is widest on **output** tokens — so
findings.input_or_condition: The stated rate table is used to justify treating output-heavy GPT work as the most favorable cheap-seat test.
findings.signal_emitted: The prior input-heavy scan is declared least able to reveal tier savings, and GPT output pricing is used as the monotonic staging rationale.
findings.truth_instead: The table gives sol/luna ratios of 20× for input, cache write, and cache read, but only 16.7× for output. Claude's corresponding ratios are equal across token kinds for a fixed seat pair, not widest on output.
findings.evidence: The target's rate table lists GPT sol/luna input as 4/0.2 and output as 20/1.2; the Claude rows scale input, reads, writes, and output proportionally.
findings.change_required: Correct the rate-ratio claim and derive task selection and host staging from the full preregistered token mix rather than output-rate ratio alone.

findings.anchor_quote: 2. **Denominator assertion.** Every run reports `items_attempted`; the harness FAILS the
findings.input_or_condition: A 40-item fixture produces a run that echoes `items_attempted: 40` after touching or verifying fewer items, or the implementation binds `N` to the Stage-1 repetition count of 3.
findings.signal_emitted: The denominator assertion is green and the run is represented as attempting the complete population.
findings.truth_instead: The source fixture contained 40 required item identities, while fewer were actually attempted or checked.
findings.evidence: The design uses `N` for both 10/40/160 items and 3/5 repetitions, and only requires a reported scalar; it never reconciles that scalar to the generator manifest, edited identities, and verifier results.
findings.change_required: Use distinct `items_per_run` and `repetitions` variables and require exact identity-set equality among the generated manifest, attempted items, and verifier receipts.

findings.anchor_quote: Report cost per **verified item** (cost ÷ items passing), never per run: an arm that
findings.input_or_condition: Repetitions have unequal pass counts and costs; for example, cheap runs of $0.10/1 pass and $90/100 passes yield $0.50 by averaging run ratios but $0.892 by ratio of sums, against an inline value of $1 per pass.
findings.signal_emitted: One allowed aggregation reports a 50% saving and fires KEEP, while another reports only a 10.8% saving.
findings.truth_instead: The design has no unique preregistered cost-per-verified-item statistic, so the threshold result is calculation-choice dependent.
findings.evidence: The quoted rule defines the within-observation ratio but does not specify ratio-of-sums, mean of ratios, paired contrast, weighting, or handling of zero-pass runs across repetitions.
findings.change_required: Preregister the cell estimator, pairing and weighting rules, zero-pass treatment, and the exact statistic to which the 20% and 25% thresholds apply.

findings.anchor_quote: 5. **Known-bad probe per check.** Following `naive_edit`: plant the wrong edit into a
findings.input_or_condition: The checker always fails because its test path is missing, collection errors, or the pristine fixture's already-failing test remains unfixed.
findings.signal_emitted: The planted edit reports MISS, so the control declares that the checker is checking and permits cells to run.
findings.truth_instead: The checker never discriminated the mutant from a faithful fix and may never have executed its subject.
findings.evidence: Task says every pristine fixture starts with a failing test. The control requires only rejection of a wrong edit and supplies no faithful-fix positive control, expected test identity/count, or infrastructure-error distinction.
findings.change_required: Require a faithful fix to pass first, mutate that known-good copy, require the intended assertion to fail, and reject runner, collection, missing-path, and wrong-test failures as control failures.

findings.anchor_quote: 5. **Known-bad probe per check.** Following `naive_edit`: plant the wrong edit into a
findings.input_or_condition: A planted wrong edit is behaviorally equivalent under the frozen interface or existing normalization, so the correct checker accepts it.
findings.signal_emitted: The control says the checker is not checking and blocks all cells.
findings.truth_instead: The checker is correct; the supposed known-bad probe was not observably bad.
findings.evidence: The rule unconditionally equates acceptance of the planted edit with a checker miss and includes no independent witness that the mutation changes required behavior.
findings.change_required: Admit a mutant only after an independent oracle proves that it fails the named behavior while the faithful fix passes; replace equivalent mutants before the instrument gate runs.

findings.anchor_quote: 4. **Zero detection.** A run reporting $0, zero output tokens, or zero items is an
findings.input_or_condition: A cheap-seat model returns a substantive refusal or abandons the task with nonzero usage but zero parsed items.
findings.signal_emitted: The design labels the observation an instrument failure and reruns, excludes, or aborts on that diagnosis.
findings.truth_instead: The instrument may be sound; zero completed items is a treatment-quality failure that must remain in the arm with its consumed cost and zero pass rate.
findings.evidence: The zero rule is unconditional and does not distinguish a receipted model outcome from absent dispatch, parser failure, or test-runner failure.
findings.change_required: Define infrastructure-failure receipts separately. Count receipted empty or partial model outcomes under intention-to-treat, including consumed cost and zero verified items.

findings.anchor_quote: 4. **Zero detection.** A run reporting $0, zero output tokens, or zero items is an
findings.input_or_condition: The new parser swaps two non-null fields, such as cache read and cache write, or double-counts reasoning as visible output.
findings.signal_emitted: All null/zero controls pass and Codex emits a plausible modelled cost and token-cause breakdown.
findings.truth_instead: The cost is wrong because cache read and write have radically different rates and reasoning/output categories overlap incorrectly.
findings.evidence: Stage 0 introduces five previously unparsed Codex kinds. The controls test presence and broad seat spread, but no bundled control asserts exact extraction and price arithmetic from a fixed usage payload.
findings.change_required: Add frozen real-shape parser goldens with exact values for all five kinds, conservation identities, both event shapes, expected modelled cost, and long-context boundary cases.

findings.anchor_quote: 6. **Fresh fixture per repetition**, so cross-run caching cannot flatter a later cell.
findings.input_or_condition: Cells run sequentially on the same model with a stable system, corpus, and task-template prefix; the run-unique identifier occurs only after that prefix.
findings.signal_emitted: A later arm's lower total is attributed to its seat or routing arm.
findings.truth_instead: The later arm was cheaper because an earlier arm paid to warm the shared prefix; a fresh suffix does not make the cache state fresh.
findings.evidence: Bundle 1 observed independent later subagents reusing a standing model prefix while the first run had 0% reuse. The target neither resets cache state nor randomizes and counterbalances arm order.
findings.change_required: Randomize and counterbalance arm order within matched blocks and either enforce independent cold cache keys, run identical warm-ups for every arm, or condition the comparison on an asserted equal cache state.

findings.anchor_quote: `cached_input_tokens` on a `spawn_agent` child's **first** request before any Codex
findings.input_or_condition: An ordinary isolated `spawn_agent` child reuses cached system/corpus tokens but receives none of the parent's conversation.
findings.signal_emitted: Nonzero cached input makes the Codex cache-key control pass and the purported fork cell is trusted.
findings.truth_instead: The tokens came from a standing shared prefix; the child was not proved to inherit the parent conversation or its cache.
findings.evidence: Bundle 2 proves a normal spawned child is conversation-isolated while receiving the whole instruction corpus. Bundle 1 separately shows standing-prefix cache reuse is available to independent agents.
findings.change_required: Use a run-unique parent-only canary absent from disk and child packets, require the child to recover it, and compare exact inherited-prefix receipts against a normal-spawn control; cached-token presence alone must not validate a fork.

findings.anchor_quote: **fork-cheap exists on Codex only.** Official Claude Code docs: a fork "inherits the full
findings.input_or_condition: The Claude `fork-same` arm silently uses an ordinary subagent or `--fork-session`, the only mechanisms demonstrated in the bundle.
findings.signal_emitted: Its cost and quality are reported as an in-process `fork-same` arm comparable to the spawn arms.
findings.truth_instead: An ordinary subagent is not a fork, while `--fork-session` is a different session-lifecycle mechanism with a different accounting boundary.
findings.evidence: Bundle 1 says four attempted `subagent_type` forks never forked, no fork appeared in the agents list, and all catalogued Claude forks were session/thread lifecycle. The target acknowledges the prior session fork is a different mechanism but specifies no Claude invocation or inheritance receipt.
findings.change_required: Name the exact supported Claude fork invocation and add a parent-only inheritance receipt. If no newly verified in-process fork exists, remove the Claude fork arm or relabel and redesign it as a session-fork treatment.

findings.anchor_quote: - **Keep the cheap seats** if delegated-to-cheap beats inline by **≥25%** cost per
findings.input_or_condition: A Stage-1 Codex cell with only three repetitions happens to show at least 25% saving and equal observed pass rate.
findings.signal_emitted: The literal KEEP condition fires because it applies at any tested size and host.
findings.truth_instead: The design itself declares N=3 insufficient for a conclusion and calls Stage 1 a screen; the effect remains unconfirmed.
findings.evidence: Immediately above the thresholds, the target says `N=3 is deliberately not enough to conclude from` and `Stage 1 is a screen, not a verdict`, but only DELETE is explicitly restricted to Stage-2 sample sizes.
findings.change_required: State that no decision threshold can fire on Stage-1 data and require an independent, completed Stage-2 N=5 confirmation before KEEP is eligible.

findings.anchor_quote: - **Keep the cheap seats** if delegated-to-cheap beats inline by **≥25%** cost per
findings.input_or_condition: At Stage 2, equal-cost populations produce one ≥25% observed winner among the many arm-size-difficulty-host contrasts, or a truly worse cheap-seat pass rate happens to look equal in five repetitions.
findings.signal_emitted: The design emits KEEP at equal-or-better quality.
findings.truth_instead: The population cost advantage can be zero and population quality inferior; the selected point estimate is sampling noise and winner selection.
findings.evidence: Bundle 1 reports five-run inline values from $0.688 to $1.260 and prior direction reversals. The threshold uses any tested cell, raw observed pass-rate ordering, no uncertainty bound, and no multiplicity adjustment.
findings.change_required: Preregister primary contrasts, paired repetition-level analysis, multiplicity control, and one-sided confidence bounds requiring the cost-saving lower bound to reach 25% and the quality non-inferiority bound to pass.

findings.anchor_quote: - **Delete them** if no delegated arm beats inline by **>20%** at any size on either
findings.input_or_condition: A cheap arm has a true saving above 20% at one size, but five noisy Stage-2 repetitions estimate every eligible contrast at 20% or less.
findings.signal_emitted: The design emits DELETE.
findings.truth_instead: A qualifying population advantage exists; failure to observe a point estimate above 20% is not evidence that every effect is at or below 20%.
findings.evidence: The design's own prior record shows large five-run spread, yet DELETE is an absence-of-observed-effect rule with no power target or upper confidence bound.
findings.change_required: Permit DELETE only when a powered analysis places the upper confidence bound for every preregistered cheap-seat contrast at or below 20%; otherwise emit inconclusive.

findings.anchor_quote: - **Delete them** if no delegated arm beats inline by **>20%** at any size on either
findings.input_or_condition: `delegated-mid` beats inline by 30%, while both delegated-cheap arms beat it by no more than 20%.
findings.signal_emitted: DELETE is not met; the result falls to inconclusive and the cheap seats stay because a delegated arm exceeded 20%.
findings.truth_instead: The mid-tier result supplies no evidence for the cheap seats whose retention is being decided.
findings.evidence: KEEP explicitly names `delegated-to-cheap`, but DELETE broadens its predicate to any `delegated arm`; the arm table includes `delegated-mid`.
findings.change_required: Make both decision branches quantify over the same explicitly enumerated cheap-seat contrasts and exclude mid-tier and fork controls from the cheap-seat delete predicate.

findings.anchor_quote: price ratio is largest there (16.7× on output), so an effect absent here is absent
findings.input_or_condition: Stage 1 observes no Codex effect, while Claude would show one because its same-model cache, fan-out behavior, TTL, model behavior, or quality response differs.
findings.signal_emitted: The design declares the effect absent everywhere and skips the Claude stage.
findings.truth_instead: Only Codex was observed; Claude can have a different sign, so its effect remains unknown.
findings.evidence: The target lists host asymmetries, and Bundle 2 measures 14–18% Codex fork caching versus 98.9% for Claude same-model fork. A larger output price ratio does not order total arm effects when token quantities and cache mechanisms differ.
findings.change_required: Run a powered Claude screen independently of the Codex outcome, or scope any null conclusion and resulting decision strictly to Codex.

findings.anchor_quote: 4b. **Cliff guard (Codex).** Peak input per run is recorded; a run above 272K input is
findings.input_or_condition: A costly cheap-arm run crosses 272K and is excluded while its matched inline run remains, or vice versa.
findings.signal_emitted: The surviving unmatched samples emit a seat saving or absence of saving at Stage-2 sample size.
findings.truth_instead: The arms are now compared on different fixture repetitions selected by a treatment-dependent post-run variable; the full route effect also includes the real cliff cost that was removed.
findings.evidence: The rule excludes `a run`, not the complete matched repetition block, and the design supplies no replacement/minimum-valid-N rule or separate cliff-inclusive estimand.
findings.change_required: Preserve the full cliff-inclusive routing result, define a separate under-cliff estimand, exclude only complete matched blocks for that estimand, and replenish blocks until every compared arm has the preregistered valid repetition count.

findings.anchor_quote: 60 files, and the single cheap-seat cell (60 files, N=2) is the only saving anywhere
findings.input_or_condition: The design's characterization of the prior cheap-seat evidence is used as written.
findings.signal_emitted: Readers are told the 60-file cheap-seat saving came from only two repetitions.
findings.truth_instead: The final prior record says all pinned cells, including the 60-file sweep cell, were N=5; only judgment cells were N=2.
findings.evidence: Bundle 1, section 2: `Baselines and the pinned cells are N=5; the judgment cells are N=2.`
findings.change_required: Correct the cited cheap-seat cell from N=2 to N=5 and revise every rationale that relies on its purported smaller denominator.

boundary_notes: Only `_parse_claude` was bundled. The implementations of `_parse_codex`, `seat_problem()`, `codex_seat_from_rollout()`, `run.py`, and `naive_edit` could not be verified; missing implementation was not treated as a defect.

External vendor documentation, current prices, field availability, and cache semantics could not be fetched. R6 findings therefore use only arithmetic and applications contained in the target and bundles.

Whether Claude gained a new in-process fork mechanism after the bundled CLI 2.1.258 record is unverified. The fork finding concerns the design's absent invocation and receipt against the bundled demonstrated mechanisms, not an external claim that no newer feature exists.

No experiment data for the proposed tasks exists yet. Statistical findings identify exact conditions under which the preregistered rules emit false decisions, using the noise and reversals reported by the design's own prior record.
